attempts.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook (run from node4, the designated control node) that publishes node2's private port-8080 app through node1 (VyOS router) so node3 can reach it, without exposing the rest of the node1<->node2 private network to node3. The private link (node1 eth1 <-> node2 ens7, previously unaddressed) was given static IPs 10.50.50.1/24 and 10.50.50.2/24; node2 got a minimal HTTP app bound only to its private IP; node1 got destination NAT (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.2:8080) plus hairpin source NAT (masquerade on eth1) so replies route back through the router, and a default-drop forward firewall with one narrow allow rule so no other port/host on the private network is reachable from node3. Verified node3 can reach the app via node1:8080 but gets 'No route to host' hitting node2's private IP directly. Diagnosed and worked around two real defects in this environment: the vyos.vyos collection's network_cli connection silently failed to persist VyOS commits, and vyos's default vbash login shell drops VyOS config-session state when SSH runs a nested plain bash -c. Fixed by using Ansible's raw module with 'sudo bash -c' (vyos has NOPASSWD ALL sudo) to run the native configure/set/commit/save sequence directly as root, verified via new commit revisions and config.boot content. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id and functional baselines on all four nodes, restarted them one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified full recovery (NAT/firewall config, private IPs, app service, and the node3->node1->node2 path) after every restart.
